title: Refinery Towns Recovered, Everyone Downstream Did Not
subtitle: Regions with their own refineries lifted purchase limits, while regions dependent on deliveries rationed fuel by the litre or by the hour.

source.name: Regional fuel availability reports from Russian and regional media

data.label: Omsk region
data.detail: Refuelling limits were lifted in full in a region hosting one of Russia's largest refineries.

data.label: Volgograd region
data.detail: Limits were lifted, then reimposed by the end of the week after the local refinery was struck again.

data.label: Bashkortostan and neighbours
data.detail: Repeated strikes on refineries around Ufa made supply difficult across the region and those next to it.

data.label: Astrakhan region
data.detail: Most filling stations now open only four to eight hours a day and refuse service outside those windows.

data.label: Novokuznetsk, Kemerovo region
data.detail: A third of filling stations in the region's second-largest city are not operating.

data.label: Novosibirsk region
data.detail: More than half of independent stations have no fuel and queues returned after the strike on the Perm refinery.

data.label: Bryansk region
data.detail: Severe per-person rationing, tightening to 20 litres closer to the border with Ukraine.

data.label: Zabaykalsky krai
data.detail: Weekly deliveries of 1,050 tons against a monthly requirement of 88,000 tons.

data.label: Chelyabinsk region
data.detail: Small farmers are struggling to source fuel during the working season.

data.label: Krasnodar krai
data.detail: Farmers received only half the fuel they needed from the state in July and drew down their own reserves.

metadata.keyFinding: Improvement was confined to refinery regions while delivery-dependent regions rationed by litre and by hour.
